summary: Aaron and his sons are appointed for priestly service, and skilled makers are directed to prepare their holy garments. Aaron's ephod and breastplate carry Israel's names, while the robe, gold forehead plate, and other clothing mark consecration and regulate approach to the holy place with explicit warnings of death.
whyItMatters: The clothing presents priestly service as carrying the people before God through a designated representative. The instructions connect beauty, memory, ritual responsibility, and the danger of approaching holiness.

context.author: Exodus does not name its final author. It records Moses writing particular covenant material; traditional Mosaic attribution and modern accounts of composition are distinguished in the book briefing.
context.audience: Israel remembering its rescue from Egypt and its obligations as a covenant community. The chapter does not identify an individual dedicatee.
context.date: The narrative places these events at Sinai after the departure from Egypt. The date of the events and the history of the book’s composition are separate, debated questions.
context.setting: The Sinai instructions for Aaron's future priestly office and the clothing of his sons.
context.literaryForm: Appointment notice and detailed vestment specifications with explanations of memorial, judgment, holiness, and protected approach.

before.text: Aaron and his sons have just been assigned to tend the lamp. The next instructions identify them more fully as priests and describe the garments for their service.

here.text: Names carried on shoulders and over the heart connect the clothing to Israel, while the closing requirements connect priestly approach to consecration and bodily covering.

after.text: The following chapter gives the washing, anointing, sacrifices, and seven-day process by which the priests are to be consecrated.

outline.heading: Priests and skilled garment makers
outline.note: Aaron’s household is chosen and the makers are endowed for holy work.

outline.heading: The ephod and shoulder memorials
outline.note: Two engraved stones carry the names of Israel on Aaron’s shoulders.

outline.heading: The breastplate and its attachments
outline.note: Twelve stones and the Urim and Thummim are carried over his heart.

outline.heading: The blue robe with bells and pomegranates
outline.note: Its construction and sound accompany Aaron’s entrance and departure.

outline.heading: The gold plate and linen garments
outline.note: The inscription identifies holiness and Aaron’s responsibility for the holy gifts.

outline.heading: Clothing and consecration for the priestly family
outline.note: The sons receive garments and linen coverings, with a warning against guilt and death.

keyVerses.text: You shall put the two stones on the shoulder straps of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel. Aaron shall bear their names before Yahweh on his two shoulders for a memorial.
keyVerses.why: The engraved shoulder stones explicitly make Aaron a bearer of Israel’s names before God.

keyVerses.text: Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment on his heart, when he goes in to the holy place, for a memorial before Yahweh continually.
keyVerses.why: The names on the breastplate repeat that representation over the priest’s heart.

keyVerses.text: They shall be on Aaron and on his sons, when they go in to the Tent of Meeting, or when they come near to the altar to minister in the holy place, that they don’t bear iniquity, and die. This shall be a statute forever to him and to his offspring after him.
keyVerses.why: The final clothing requirement attaches the possibility of guilt and death to priestly approach.

questions.question: Why are skilled makers mentioned with the priestly appointment?
questions.answer: God directs those filled with wisdom to make garments that consecrate Aaron for service. Craft ability contributes directly to preparing the priest for that office.

questions.question: What is the “ephod” in these instructions?
questions.answer: It is a priestly garment with shoulder straps and a woven band, made from gold and colored linen work. Its shoulder pieces hold engraved stones, and the breastplate is attached to it; the passage does not require a complete modern tailoring pattern to understand those functions.

questions.question: How do the two sets of engraved stones differ?
questions.answer: Two shoulder stones divide the names six and six in birth order, while the breastplate has twelve individually named stones in four rows. Both are explained as carrying Israel before God, first on Aaron's shoulders and then on his heart.

questions.question: Does the chapter explain how the Urim and Thummim work?
questions.answer: It commands that they be placed in the breastplate of judgment and associates them with bearing Israel's judgment before God. Their physical form and the procedure for consulting them are not explained in this chapter.

questions.question: Why do the robe’s bells matter?
questions.answer: Their sound is to be heard as Aaron enters and leaves the holy place, and the text links that requirement with not dying. It states the serious consequence without explaining a mechanical or magical process by which the sound protects him.

questions.question: What does the forehead plate say and accomplish in the instructions?
questions.answer: It is engraved HOLY TO YAHWEH, and Aaron is said to bear the iniquity of Israel's holy gifts so that they may be accepted. The wording assigns ritual responsibility but does not specify every possible fault in an offering or turn the priest into a morally faultless person.

questions.question: Why end with linen pants and a warning of death?
questions.answer: They cover the naked body from waist to thighs during approach to the tent or altar. The text treats adequate clothing as a serious condition of service, with guilt and death named explicitly; it does not present this simply as a matter of personal taste.

glossary.def: The elaborate priestly garment with shoulder straps and a woven band to which the breastplate is attached.
The square doubled piece carrying twelve named stones and the Urim and Thummim.
Set apart Aaron and his sons for the specified priestly service.
